title: Lahanorizo
subtitle: Greek cabbage and rice in olive oil and tomato
excerpt: White cabbage and long-grain rice cooked together in tomato and extra-virgin olive oil. A frugal Greek one-pot that is deeply savoury despite its short ingredients list.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek ladera dish, common in Lent and everyday home cooking. Synthesised from multiple Greek home cook sources.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a large wide pot. Add extra stock if the mixture looks dry.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: Lahanorizo is a Greek ladera dish: everything cooked in a generous amount of olive oil. The cabbage gives a lot of liquid as it cooks, which the rice absorbs. Use a good fruity olive oil as it is a main flavour, not just a cooking fat.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the shredded cabbage and stir to coat. Cook on a medium heat for 5 minutes until it wilts and reduces in volume.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Add the rinsed rice and stir once. Cover and cook on a low heat for 20 minutes. Do not lift the lid during this time.
Check that the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. If not, cover for 5 more minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the lemon juice and dill. Rest for 5 minutes, then drizzle with extra olive oil before serving.

items.cause: There was not enough liquid, or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Add 100ml of hot water, cover and cook for a further 5 to 8 minutes on a medium-low heat.

items.symptom: The rice has turned to mush.
items.cause: Too much liquid or it cooked too long.
items.fix: Keep to the quantity of stock given. Check at 20 minutes and remove from heat as soon as the rice is just tender.

items.cause: Not enough lemon or the olive oil was too neutral.
items.fix: Add more lemon juice and a generous drizzle of a good fruity extra-virgin olive oil at the end.
